88b3c7b4a51c: 150+ properties sounds like a project. It is a wizard of four steps that fills in the likely choices for you, with a live preview before you save anything.
6e19fcdb6404: Most Salesforce components with real depth make you learn them twice: once to understand the properties, once to remember which combination you picked last time. The Setup Wizard exists so you do neither. It asks where the calendar goes and what each pick should save, fills in the fields it can work out, writes the configuration as metadata, and hands you a name you can use anywhere.

c4b6e66fccec: <t1>One record per day, or per range?</t1> Monday through Friday for six weeks can be thirty records or six.
fe4ecaf3906b: <t1>One record per time block, or one with breaks inside?</t1> A training day with a lunch break can be two records or one plus a break.
b6936b1df041: <t1>Booking a room or person?</t1> One at a time, several at once, or add one to a range, a time block or a day with breaks.

6ef1b91add49: Saving deploys a Custom Metadata record. Three things follow:
76f3f8569399: <t1>It is deployable.</t1> Custom Metadata moves through your normal release pipeline, sandbox to production, like any other component.
63a06b08012d: <t1>It is reusable.</t1> Put the name in <t2>Config Name</t2> on any component and it picks up the whole configuration. One config, many placements.
9b6997413616: <t1>It stays in your org.</t1> Nothing is stored on a vendor server, so the configuration is yours and it is visible in Setup.
93a44bd7e810: <t1>About the deploy.</t1> Custom Metadata deploys are asynchronous. The wizard waits about two minutes and then, if the record has not appeared, shows you the deploy id and a link to Setup → Deployment Status. A busy org can take longer than the wizard waits, and the deploy still finishes.
8783c0f0371c: <t1>Who can run it.</t1> Assign <t2>MultiDatePick - Setup</t2> to admins who build configs. It includes the Setup Wizard. Everyone who uses the calendars gets <t3>MultiDatePick - User</t3>, and <t4>MultiDatePick - All Access</t4> covers both.
3ed427a37e1b: Import, export, and the mapping step people miss
3edd4a249d14: The Import / Export tab takes a JSON configuration and turns it into a saved config. That is how the <t1>Config Library</t1> works: 47 ready-made configurations covering time-off requests, room booking, hot-desking, shift rosters, fleet reservation and more.
052365d2aeba: From the Config Library to a working Lightning page: copy, paste, deploy, drop the component on the page and give it the config name.
016939a477ec: The step that saves the most time is the <t1>guided import</t1>. Library configs reference the demo objects; your org has its own names, and the import expects that. The moment you paste, it asks four plain questions, each already answered with the closest match in your org: which objects hold the bookings and what is booked, which of your fields does each job (the day, the start time, the status), which of your status values mean the same as the config's, and which button Flows to keep or skip. Change any answer, click <t2>Apply & Deploy</t2>, and it deploys with the rewritten JSON. No text editor, no hunt and replace, no re-uploads.
db0ca063fdc8: Pick your objects and every field and status value is matched by type and name. Change any answer that looks wrong.
08e5d77cab36: Export works the same way in reverse, which makes configurations shareable. A config that works in one org is a paste away from working in another.
63b7a1e97dee: Using the config once it exists
f9b64daaf35a: Drop any of the three components onto a Lightning record page, app page, Home page or Experience Cloud site, set <t1>Config Name</t1> to the name you chose, and leave every other property blank. The config supplies them. On App, Home and Experience pages, put the parent record in <t2>Static Parent Record Id</t2>.
66794ce291b9: The same applies inside a Screen Flow: put the config's name in <t1>Config Name</t1> and every on/off setting comes from the config. You do not set a single checkbox in Flow Builder; the few flow-only ones (Required, Show Inline) are off unless you turn them on. Pass the parent record into <t2>Parent Record Id</t2>.
